key_insight: Cu-based ternary chalcogenides like Cu2SiSe3 and Cu2SnS3 can significantly enhance photovoltaic performance in tandem solar cell architectures.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a simpler alternative to quaternary chalcogenides, contributing to the sustainability of solar technologies.
method: Drift diffusion modeling was utilized to assess device performance.
Absorber layer characteristics such as thickness and defect density were analyzed.
The impact of buffer layers on device efficiency was explored.
evidence_signal: The optimized single junction devices demonstrated power conversion efficiencies of 18.13% for Cu2SiSe3 and 15.59% for Cu2SnS3, with advancements noted in tandem cell configurations.
watch_item: Further investigation is needed to ensure long-term stability and scalability of the tandem solar cell design.
paper_title: Photovoltaic Possibility of Cu2SiSe3 and Cu2SnS3 Ternary Chalcogenides- Single Junction to Tandem Architecture
